status: Quality owner native read/decision and native cancellation slice. Workspace/detail decisions over quality-owned relations and one owner-local HTTP/Next transport are implemented; the cancellation command preserves CAS, independence, local idempotency, rollback and persisted readback. Hold/inspection/release/disposition/specification writes and cross-owner presentation labels remain retained. No browser journey is claimed.

scope.domain: packages/server-quality/src/domain/quality.rs owns hold/inspection/cancellation statuses, measurement evaluation, release/cancellation/disposition decision derivation, retained next-action copy, reason bounds and the uninspected-hold/independent-review cancellation plan.
scope.application: packages/server-quality/src/application/quality.rs owns current quality.read authorization, Company/branch/department scope, workspace/detail views and the cancellation use case. Neither layer mints IAM, purchase or Workflow authority.
scope.adapters: packages/server-quality/src/adapters/quality_read.rs reads only Quality-owned relations (inventory_quality_holds, inspections, measurements, specifications, spec metrics, cancellations, disposition events and alerts) inside a caller-owned serializable transaction. It locks those relations, bounds every read, keeps a database/backend/xid/postmaster snapshot with require_current, and applies the native cancellation update plus immutable cancellation row. Cross-owner stock, lot, product, warehouse, attachment, Finance, Inventory-count and notification facts were not added as SQL.
scope.http: packages/server-quality/src/adapters/quality_http.rs exposes GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/quality, GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/quality/{id} and POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/quality/{id}/cancel. It validates exact registered host/slug targets, origin, one Idempotency-Key, JSON content type, bounded body, paths and owner error mapping. Session resolution, current Company scope, purchase admission and the owner transaction stay behind QualityHttpBackend.
scope.frontend: packages/feature-quality/src/adapters/server/native-quality.ts is an opt-in loopback transport for ERPX_NATIVE_QUALITY_CONFIG. Unset configuration keeps the retained Quality reader. Configured transport, authority or response failures close with 503 NATIVE_QUALITY_UNAVAILABLE and never retry the retained reader. The Quality workspace/detail presenters and Quality route overlay native decision flags and, when configured, send cancellation through the native command. Native cancellation is preceded by the retained Commercial purchase/current-authority preflight in native-quality-owned.ts.
notNativeYet: Manual hold creation, inspection, release, scrap disposition, specification create/activate/cancel and alert acknowledgement remain the retained TypeScript writers because they compose Inventory stock/lot facts, Files evidence, Workflow receipts, Finance and/or Inventory count posting.
Workspace stock, lot, product, specification labels, eligible recipient counts and attachment metadata remain retained TypeScript reads. No native Commerce/Inventory presentation port was added.
Quality work projection, inbox/calendar handoffs and the due/overdue alert sweep remain retained.

behavior.readScope: quality.read is required and a department-scoped assignment returns 403 QUALITY_SCOPE_REQUIRED before the repository. Company is mandatory; an optional branch filter is applied in SQL. Foreign Company and out-of-branch detail ids return QUALITY_HOLD_NOT_FOUND.
behavior.readUnit: The adapter requires an active transaction and SERIALIZABLE isolation (QUALITY_TRANSACTION_REQUIRED / QUALITY_SERIALIZABLE_REQUIRED), takes a SHARE lock on the eight Quality-owned relations, and retains the transaction/database identity. require_current re-reads the workspace or detail and returns 409 QUALITY_READ_CHANGED on any concurrent change.
behavior.readBounds: At most 1000 holds, 1000 inspections, 5000 measurements, 1000 specification metrics, 200 cancellations, 200 disposition events and 1000 alerts are admitted; overflow returns 503 QUALITY_READ_LIMIT. Every integer is checked against the JavaScript safe-integer boundary.
behavior.inspectionResults: Evaluate one value for every captured metric, reject duplicates/unknown or missing metrics (QUALITY_MEASUREMENTS_REQUIRED), derive pass/fail from the min/max limits, reject a conflicting requested result (QUALITY_RESULT_DERIVED), require an explicit result without a specification (QUALITY_RESULT_REQUIRED), and reject measurements on a hold without a specification (QUALITY_SPEC_REQUIRED).
behavior.releaseAndCancellationDecisions: The hold creator cannot inspect; release requires awaiting_release + pass + quality.release + a different creator and inspector; cancellation is offered only on an uninspected held hold; cancellation review requires cancel_pending + quality.release + a different creator and requester; failed stock offers disposition only to an independent quality.release holder. The detail next-action copy mirrors the retained presenter.
behavior.cancellation: The native writer checks the current Company/branch, expected version and the uninspected-hold invariant. request moves held to cancel_pending; approve moves cancel_pending to cancelled with cancelled_by/cancelled_at; reject returns cancel_pending to held. Every accepted action inserts one immutable inventory_quality_cancellations row at expected_version + 1. The writer checks exact ids and the IAM-owned iam_same_person merged-identity fact before an approve/reject, so a merged alias cannot review its own request. The update is a compare-and-swap on id, company, expected version and source status.
behavior.idempotency: A cancellation id is derived as quality-cancel-{Idempotency-Key}. Repeating the same key, actor, hold, action and reason returns the saved receipt without a second event; reusing the key with different facts returns 409 QUALITY_CANCELLATION_CONFLICT. This is owner-local replay only; Workflow command receipts and audit/outbox retention remain a composition obligation.
behavior.quarantine: Reject restores the hold to held rather than releasing stock. The existing database quarantine triggers remain authoritative; no Quality read or cancellation path writes commerce_stock, inventory_lots, command_receipts, audit_events or outbox_events.
behavior.transport: Native responses are camelCase envelopes ({data: ...}) with Cache-Control: private, no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Unknown target, duplicate/foreign host, foreign origin, missing/duplicate key, non-JSON body, malformed payload and owner errors map to 404/422/403/409/503 as appropriate.

limits: No authenticated browser journey was run. Do not claim browser verification from this evidence.

The native HTTP router is not mounted in the running composition; it is proven by a loopback transport test with a reference backend. A composed HTTP+PostgreSQL test remains blocked by the prohibition on editing src/composition/Cargo.toml and src/composition/**.

The native read deliberately omits product/warehouse/lot names, stock/lot options, attachment descriptors and eligible-recipient counts. The Quality pages still require the retained reader for those labels; only decision flags and the cancellation command are native.

The native cancellation writer is reached in this slice by the owner adapter and route preflight, not by a composed session/current-IAM unit. The composition backend must recheck purchase, current authority and Workflow receipt/outbox in the same transaction.

The native read decision overlay uses exact user ids for independence. Merged IAM aliases are enforced at the native cancellation write by iam_same_person, but the read-only decision flags remain advisory and are not a substitute for the write guard.

The detail page reads retained labels/history before the native decision. If the two versions differ, the page uses the native version and flags but does not refetch the retained history in the same request; the native version prevents a stale action gate.
The existing consumption_postgres suite still covers initial-count history and stock-consumption hold decisions; it was not replaced by this slice.
